open_points.subject: AdmissionVerdict identity and repeated admission
open_points.text: “Substitution: a verdict for the same implementation and corpus is the same verdict.” conflicts with “every active case of the corpus is run again for the implementation at admission time, and the verdict covers exactly those executions.”
open_points.question: When the same implementation is submitted again against an unchanged corpus, is there one immutable AdmissionVerdict or a new verdict associated with the newly created TrialExecutions?
options: Reuse the original verdict and leave the new TrialExecutions outside it
Replace or mutate the existing verdict so it names the new TrialExecutions
Create a distinct AdmissionVerdict for each admission run
open_points.default_guess: Create a distinct admission record for each submission so each record names exactly the executions that produced it.

open_points.subject: Mapped FlowNode port cardinality
open_points.text: M01 says “an edge requires both ports to carry the same schema, the same carriage and, for files, the same media type” and defines `many` as what a map runs over, while M14 says “the one input port a `many` edge maps the node over” is delivered one element at a time and “each output collects one result per element.”
open_points.question: What cardinalities do the mapped input during each invocation and the collected mapped outputs have, and is mapping an exception to ordinary edge cardinality equality?
options: A `many` source maps into a `one` node input, and every collected output is effectively `many`
The target input remains `many`, with each element wrapped as a one-element collection
Mapped nodes have a separate persisted effective interface describing mapped input and output cardinalities
open_points.default_guess: Treat mapping as an explicit exception: a `many` source feeds one element into a `one` input per invocation, and each output becomes an effective `many` collection.

open_points.subject: Capture of failures after a non-failed terminal run
open_points.text: K-10 says a run’s spool “is emptied when the run ends — except a `failed` run,” but the capture action refuses only when “the run was already released (its files are gone),” and M06 likewise excludes only an execution “whose run was already released.”
open_points.question: Can a failed function execution be captured after its run ended `refused` or `cancelled`, when file inputs needed for the trial fixture have already been removed?
options: Refuse capture whenever any referenced spooled bytes are no longer present
Retain the spool for every run containing a capturable failed function execution
Allow capture after such runs only when all captured inputs are durable value-carriage inputs
open_points.default_guess: Allow capture only when all required inputs still exist; refuse a file-bearing capture after any spool removal.

open_points.subject: Cancellation during an active node attempt
open_points.text: The action says “cancel a run” and “the run ends `cancelled`; nothing further is sent,” with failure only for “a finished run,” but NodeExecution has no cancelled or interrupted status and EffectAttempt does not say what cancellation does to an `in_flight` attempt.
open_points.question: What happens when the owner cancels a `running` run while a function, read operation, or effect send is already in progress?
options: Cancellation is handled only at safe boundaries and cannot overlap an active attempt
Active work is allowed to finish, but no new work is scheduled before the run becomes `cancelled`
Active work is aborted and receives a defined interrupted status; an in-flight effect becomes `unknown`
open_points.default_guess: Process cancellation at a safe boundary, preserve the concluded outcome of work already started, and schedule nothing further.

open_points.subject: Recovery of a persisted running run
open_points.text: M27 names “start-up recovery” as kernel activity and M26 defines recovery for effect attempts, but no text says what recovery does to a Run persisted as `running` with an unfinished function or read-operation attempt.
open_points.question: After process restart, how does the kernel transition or continue a run that was actively executing something for which no EffectAttempt exists?
options: Retry unfinished pure functions and read operations automatically
Record the interrupted function or read operation as failed and end or advance the run accordingly
Leave the run `running` until a new explicit recovery or resume action is defined
open_points.default_guess: Record the interrupted work as a failed execution and advance the run to its corresponding final or remaining-branch state; only an in-flight effect is recovered as `unknown`.

open_points.subject: Run creation with invalid flow inputs
open_points.text: M19 says a run contains validated “`inputs`: StoredValues (M21) by flow input port,” while the `run a flow` action specifies no outcome for missing, extra, or schema-invalid input values.
open_points.question: Does an invalid set of flow inputs refuse the start without creating a Run, or create a Run that ends in failure, and where is the validation failure recorded?
options: Refuse the start and create no Run
Create a Run that immediately becomes `failed`
Create a Run plus a synthetic NodeExecution or other trace record for flow-input validation
open_points.default_guess: Validate all flow inputs before minting the run and refuse the start without creating a Run.
